final_span:
tucked under his pocket a toothbrush and a Slinky from the National Museum of American History.
On the way to the moon, Armstrong detached the toothbrush from its box, and read an inscription. It honored President Harry S. Truman, who presented the boxed brush to the Museum following the loss of his tooth. The note read “Give a man a toothbrush and you feed his spirit.” Armstrong then tucked the toothbrush back whence it came.
During the return trip, Armstrong requested that Buzz Aldrin, his fellow crew member and pilot, take a thorough gaze at the moon.
